text: DEFONEOS — DEFRA Drinking Water Inspectorate Regulatory Reform AI Deep-Dive Pack EU AI Act Article 50 live 2 Aug 2026 — C2PA passport ready | Get yours → Home Master GovBench Index Sitemap DEFONEOS × DEFRA × DWI DEFRA Drinking Water Inspectorate Regulatory Reform AI Deep-Dive Pack Sovereign AI governance of UK DWI regulatory reform — water quality enforcement, supply network regulation, compliance monitoring, private supply oversight, PFAS monitoring, lead pipe replacement, water company performance. 12 entry points × 8 transformation priorities × 6 MCPs. Audit-grade. Signed. UK-sovereign. 12 Entry Points 8 Transformation Priorities 6 MCP Servers 6 Red Lines 📋 12 Entry Points Enforcement Enforcement Powers — Criminal Sanctions, Prosecution, Penalties DWI enforcement framework — Water Industry Act 1991. Criminal prosecution for supply failures. Enforcement notices. Improvement plans. Financial penalties — Water Services Regulation Authority (Ofwat). Prosecution for water quality failures. DWI Chief Inspector annual report. Statutory duty to supply wholesome water. Emergency prohibitions. Boil water notices. Monitoring Compliance Monitoring — Sampling, Testing, Reporting Water quality monitoring programme — 4.8M samples annually. Chemical, microbiological, aesthetic parameters. DWI audit of water company laboratories. Sampling frequency requirements. Compliance assessment — individual and system compliance. Investigative monitoring for failures. Customer contact trigger sampling. Emergency response sampling. Third-party laboratory accreditation (UKAS). PFAS PFAS Monitoring — Forever Chemicals, Risk Assessment Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) — emerging contaminant class. Drinking water standard: 100ng/l aggregate. PFAS source identification — firefighting foam, industrial discharge. Water company PFAS monitoring programme. Treatment technology assessment — GAC, ion exchange, RO. Risk assessment for catchment areas. International comparison — EU, US EPA standards. PFAS health effects research integration. Lead Lead Pipe Replacement — Programme, Compliance, Funding Lead pipe replacement programme — target: all lead pipes replaced by 2050. Estimated 6-10M lead service pipes in England and Wales. Water company investment programme — AMP8. Customer engagement — lead awareness, free testing. Lead monitoring — 25 µg/l action level, 10 µg/l target. Phosphate dosing as interim measure. Priority areas — schools, hospitals, childcare. Funding mechanisms — Ofwat, water company investment. Private Supplies Private Supplies — Regulation, Risk Assessment, Enforcement Private water supplies — 97,000+ in England. Local authority regulation. Risk assessment programme — Type A (commercial), Type B (single dwelling), Type C (large). Monitoring requirements by risk category. Enforcement notices. Treatment requirements. Funding — private supply grants. Tenant protection. Agricultural contamination risk. Legionella risk. EU Drinking Water Directive alignment. Cyber Cyber Security — Operational Technology, SCADA, Resilience Water sector cyber security — NCSC guidance. Operational technology (OT) protection — SCADA, PLCs, telemetry. Supply chain cyber risk. Incident reporting — NCSC, ICO. Resilience testing. Network segmentation. Legacy system security. IT/OT convergence risks. NIS Regulations compliance. National Security Act implications. Water company cyber maturity assessment. Resilience Supply Resilience — Drought, Flooding, Infrastructure Water supply resilience — drought planning, demand management. Infrastructure resilience — treatment works, reservoirs, distribution network. Climate change adaptation — rainfall patterns, demand growth. Emergency supply planning — tankers, bowsers, alternative sources. Cross-border supply agreements. Water transfer schemes. Strategic resource options. Regional resilience assessment.
